From c32b26aaa2f9216520a38b3f4bfeec846eb3eb8a Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Tristan Madani <tristan@talencesecurity.com>
Date: Wed, 27 May 2026 13:57:50 +0000
Subject: [PATCH] netfilter: nft_tunnel: fix use-after-free on object destroy

nft_tunnel_obj_destroy() calls metadata_dst_free() which directly
kfree()s the metadata_dst, ignoring the dst_entry refcount. Packets
that took a reference via dst_hold() in nft_tunnel_obj_eval() and
are still queued (e.g. in a netem qdisc) are left with a dangling
pointer. When these packets are eventually dequeued, dst_release()
operates on freed memory.

Replace metadata_dst_free() with dst_release() so the metadata_dst
is freed only after all references are dropped. The dst subsystem
already handles metadata_dst cleanup in dst_destroy() when
DST_METADATA is set.

Fixes: af308b94a2a4 ("netfilter: nf_tables: add tunnel support")
Cc: stable@vger.kernel.org
Signed-off-by: Tristan Madani <tristan@talencesecurity.com>
Reviewed-by: Fernando Fernandez Mancera <fmancera@suse.de>
Signed-off-by: Florian Westphal <fw@strlen.de>
Signed-off-by: Pablo Neira Ayuso <pablo@netfilter.org>

diff --git a/net/netfilter/nft_tunnel.c b/net/netfilter/nft_tunnel.c
index 0b987bc2132a..68f7cfbbee06 100644
--- a/net/netfilter/nft_tunnel.c
+++ b/net/netfilter/nft_tunnel.c
@@ -676,7 +676,7 @@ static void nft_tunnel_obj_destroy(const struct nft_ctx *ctx,
 {
 	struct nft_tunnel_obj *priv = nft_obj_data(obj);
 
-	metadata_dst_free(priv->md);
+	dst_release(&priv->md->dst);
 }
 
 static struct nft_object_type nft_tunnel_obj_type;
-- 
2.34.1

## Summary of Modifications

### Files modified:
- `net/netfilter/nft_tunnel.c` (one-line change in `nft_tunnel_obj_destroy`)

### Modification:
In the function `nft_tunnel_obj_destroy`, the call:
```c
metadata_dst_free(priv->md);
```
was replaced with:
```c
dst_release(&priv->md->dst);
```

### Rationale (relationship between the change and the bug):
The bug was a **use-after-free** vulnerability. The original code used `metadata_dst_free()`, which unconditionally frees the `metadata_dst` structure via `kfree()`, disregarding any outstanding references held by packets still in transit (e.g., packets queued in a netem qdisc). Those packets had previously incremented the `dst_entry` refcount via `dst_hold()` in `nft_tunnel_obj_eval()`. When the tunnel object was destroyed, the metadata destination was freed immediately, leaving those packets with a dangling pointer. Upon later dequeuing, `dst_release()` would operate on freed memory, causing a use-after-free.

The fix replaces the unconditional free with `dst_release()`, which decrements the reference count of the embedded `dst_entry`. Only when all references are dropped (including those held by packets) will `dst_destroy()` be called, and because the `DST_METADATA` flag is set, the metadata-specific cleanup (including freeing the `metadata_dst`) is handled correctly by the destination subsystem. This ensures the memory is freed only after no packets reference it, thus preventing the use-after-free.

netfilter: nft_tunnel: fix use-after-free on object destroy

nft_tunnel_obj_destroy() calls metadata_dst_free() which directly
kfree()s the metadata_dst, ignoring the dst_entry refcount. Packets
that took a reference via dst_hold() in nft_tunnel_obj_eval() and
are still queued (e.g. in a netem qdisc) are left with a dangling

already handles metadata_dst cleanup in dst_destroy() when

Fixes: af308b94a2a4 ("netfilter: nf_tables: add tunnel support")
Cc: stable@vger.kernel.org
Signed-off-by: Tristan Madani <tristan@talencesecurity.com>
Reviewed-by: Fernando Fernandez Mancera <fmancera@suse.de>
Signed-off-by: Florian Westphal <fw@strlen.de>

Here is the root cause:
The `nft_tunnel_obj_destroy` function called `metadata_dst_free()` which directly frees the `metadata_dst` structure without considering the `dst_entry` reference count. Packets that had taken a reference via `dst_hold()` in `nft_tunnel_obj_eval()` and were still queued (e.g., in a netem qdisc) retained a dangling pointer after the object was destroyed. When those packets were later dequeued, `dst_release()` operated on freed memory, causing a use-after-free.

Here is the patch:
 
 static void nft_tunnel_obj_destroy(const struct nft_ctx *ctx,
 				   struct nft_object *obj)
 {
 	struct nft_tunnel_obj *priv = nft_obj_data(obj);
 
-	metadata_dst_free(priv->md);
+	dst_release(&priv->md->dst);
 }
